$comment: THE SINGLE INDEX OF THE DOCUMENTATION. Phase 0 of plans/documentation-wiki.md.
This file replaces six hand-maintained lists that had drifted apart: the CLAUDE.md index table,
docs/user-guide/README.md's contents table, examples/README.md, src/main/docs.ts's REFERENCE_PAGES
(the in-app operator sidebar), scripts/build-docs-html.cjs's PAGES, and the future site sidebar.
Every one of them was a place a new chapter could be forgotten, and at least one of them was already
wrong: build-docs-html.cjs's list ended at '13-keyboard-reference.md', a file that does not exist, so
the built guide silently dropped the Tracking and Show chapters.
scripts/verify-docs.cjs enforces this file against the tree, and it runs inside `npm run verify`.

hybrid  the page is 'architecture AND usage' in one file. Ships in the app today; Phase 2 marks
its operator regions with <!-- audience:operator --> so the operator view can be assembled
from it WITHOUT copying the prose into a second file that would then drift.
code    written for whoever BUILDS ArtLux. NEVER reachable from the in-app operator sidebar and

Adding a doc? Add it here, or `npm run verify` fails. That is the point.
$referenceOrder: KEY ORDER IS THE READING ORDER, and src/main/docs.ts renders the operator sidebar in it. Do not
sort this block alphabetically or group it by tag: the previous hand-kept list opened with the
Feature & Usage Guide, and the first tag-grouped version of this file opened the sidebar with
'Video codecs — HAP & MP4/WebCodecs', which is not where anyone starts. The order below is the
arc an operator actually travels: orient -> install -> the workspace -> content -> time -> the
show -> outputs -> fixtures -> projectors -> protocols -> tracking -> running it unattended.

generated.why: Chapter 15 was hand-typed, was edited as recently as 2026-07-28, and STILL documented the static list SHORTCUTS.md says was replaced. Re-typing a registry loses that race every time.

The uniforms a shader can read are declared once, in the wrapper that injects them. A hand-kept table is wrong the first time one is added, and a reference listing a uniform the wrapper does not declare sends an author hunting a compile error in their own code.

The guide teaches with SHIPPED shaders — four are in the app dropdown and all are compiled on a real driver before release. Copying them into markdown by hand would break that the first time one was edited.
Ten noise generators, each compiled on a real driver by the release harness. A noise function that does not build is worse than none, because it is copied before it is tested.

verifiedAgainstSource.why: The doc table carries argument types and prose the switch does not, so it is CHECKED both ways rather than generated. That check found /scene/recall and /cue/fire handled in source and documented nowhere.
EFFECT_NAMES has only the names; the doc adds what each speed/intensity knob does. Generating it would DELETE information, so it is checked, not generated.
